subject: Commit ladder proposal and smoothing options for hosted API consumption
messages:
From: Naveen Sharma <naveen@clario.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify commit ladder and smoothing credits

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the draft pricing you shared in the call yesterday. Procurement is trying to map your breakpoints to our burn profile and we have a couple of questions before we go to legal:

- Are your discounts marginal (only the incremental tokens at breakpoint get the discount) or blended (all tokens billed at the new effective rate)?
- Do you offer a smoothing/rolling mechanism (30/60d) so we don't get hit by a short-term spike? If so, how are the credits applied?
- If we commit to a tier but underdeliver for the quarter, what is the true-up? Any overcommit credit?

I attached our 6‑month usage estimates (clario_volume_estimates.xlsx). Can you provide two customer-facing options we can circulate: one for a predictability-oriented finance team (they prefer a blended effective rate) and one for a product-led team that prefers aggressive marginal breakpoints?

Thanks,
Naveen
Naveen Sharma
Head of Platform Procurement
Clario Health
procurement@clario.com
(415) 555-0123
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Naveen Sharma <naveen@clario.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify commit ladder and smoothing credits

Hi Naveen — appreciate the detailed estimates, got the spreadsheet. High level answers below and I'll attach a one-page summary for Procurement.

1) Marginal vs blended:
- We can do either. Marginal gives better upside to you when usage is concentrated above breakpoints; blended gives predictability and is simpler to forecast for finance.

2) Smoothing / rolling window:
- We offer a 30-day rolling smoothing policy by default for hosted API customers on commit tiers: spikes are averaged across the window and overage is prorated; we also provide a one-time smoothing credit for the first quarter if historical usage is noisy.

3) Underdeliver / true-up:
- Standard: quarterly true-up at the base rate with an earned-commit credit structure. We can offer an overcommit credit (applied as usage credits against the next quarter) equal to 25% of unearned commit for the first year.

Attached: Redwood_Commit_Ladder_v1.pdf — it has two customer-facing options ("Predictable Blended" and "Variable Marginal") plus a worked example using your estimates.

I'll loop in Laura and Ben for the effective-rate math and any finance guardrails. Can you confirm whether Clario prefers billing monthly or quarterly for true-ups?

Best,
Jonas

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify commit ladder and smoothing credits (internal)

Jonas / Ben — quick notes from a pricing perspective before we send anything final to Clario. I'm recommending we offer two discrete options with clear tradeoffs: 

Option A — Predictable Blended (recommended for finance-heavy buyers):
- Commit tiers: 0–500M tokens, 500M–1.5B, >1.5B
- Effective blended discounts: 0%, 12%, 20% (applied to full consumption once breakpoint is reached)
- Quarterly billing; monthly reporting; 60-day lookback smoothing credit available at 1x for first Q
- Pros: simple forecast, predictable invoice. Cons: slightly higher cost at low volumes vs marginal.

Option B — Variable Marginal (recommended for product teams expecting spikes):
- Breakpoints (marginal): 0–500M @ list, 500M–1.5B @ list*0.88 (12% off marginal), >1.5B @ list*0.80 (20% off marginal)
- 30-day rolling smoothing (averages spikes); true-up monthly
- Overcommit safeguard: if commit missed by >20% for the quarter, apply 25% unearned-commit credit to next quarter
- Pros: best possible unit economics when usage grows. Cons: more complex invoicing math.

Worked example (from their spreadsheet): with a 900M actuals month, blended option yields an "effective" rate ~11% better than base; marginal yields 9% improvement but only on incremental tokens. We should include both effective-rate numbers in the customer doc.

Finance guardrail: we need a clear floor (net effective price) so we don't go below our hosting marginal cost. Ben, can you confirm the floor we should pass to legal (and whether the 25% overcommit credit is acceptable)?

-Laura
Laura Bennett | Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Laura — quick confirmation from SRE/finance side: the floor we can accept for this deal is list minus 28% (i.e., 72% of list) as a 12-month committed effective net floor. That gives us headroom for quantization and batch gains. The proposed 25% overcommit credit is fine for year 1; after that, scale-dependent.

Two practical notes: 
- For blended proposals, include a worked calculation showing effective blended rate and monthly invoice example. Clario's finance team will want to see the monthly true-up math.
- For marginal ladder, include a one-line table showing marginal rate per bracket and a short example row (e.g., 900M tokens -> X tokens billed at list, Y at 12% off, etc.).

I can draft the example table and pass to Jonas to include in the customer doc.

—Ben

Hi Naveen — thanks for the patience while we lined up internal approvals. Per our conversation, attached is a short customer-ready one-pager (Redwood_Commit_Ladder_v1.pdf) and an example billing worksheet. Summary of the two options: 

Option 1 — Predictable Blended (best for Finance):
- Tiers: 0–500M, 500M–1.5B, >1.5B
- Blended effective discounts: 0%, 12%, 20% (applies to full consumption once tier hit)
- Quarterly true-up; 60-day smoothing credit available first Q; monthly reporting
- Result: predictable invoicing and straightforward forecasting

Option 2 — Variable Marginal (best for Product):
- Marginal discounts at breakpoints: 12% for 500M–1.5B, 20% for >1.5B (only incremental tokens receive the discount)
- 30-day rolling smoothing applied, monthly true-up
- 25% overcommit credit applied to next quarter if commit missed in Q1
- Result: lower unit costs when usage grows aggressively, slightly more complex invoice math

Ask: which option should I have Legal produce redlines for? If you'd like, we can (A) go blended with a 60-day smoothing credit to start (fast approval path) or (B) go marginal with a 25% overcommit safeguard (preferred by product).

Next steps: once you confirm preferred option and billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly true-up), I'll open a DocuSign with the chosen term sheet and include the example invoice for Finance to review.
